newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage-backed prepay fears subside in rate spike.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage-backed prepay fears subside in rate spike.

text.p: A nosedive in U.S. Treasuries for the second straight Friday left mortgage-backed securities (MBS) looking relatively attractive as prepayment fears were further alleviated.
A prepayment hedge trade was partially reversed during this interest rate spike. Traders observed Treasuries being unloaded while MBS were being purchased.

As a result, current coupon 7-1/2 percent MBS fell a maximum of 5/8 point, while 10-year Treasuries plunged nearly one point. The plummeting dollar, technical selling and swaps out of Treasuries spurred the steep sell-off, traders said.
"This was a good up-in-coupon day," said Kenneth Willmann, vice president of mutual fund portfolios at USAA Investment Management in San Antonio, Texas.
Prior to last Friday's rate surge, down-in-coupon MBS trades prevailed. Investors had been selling higher-coupon MBS that were prepay-sensitive and instead buying discount MBS.

"Probably what they wish they had done was sold Treasuries yesterday and held cash until buying MBS today," Willmann said. Still, "one day is not a trend," he said, adding: "I have not done anything in the fund today. I haven't made any core-type purchases or sales."
The up-in-coupon strategy, amid lessening prepayment risks, was clear when assessing MBS price changes Friday.
Thirty-year MBS with eight percent and higher coupons were unchanged to 3/8 point lower at most. Lower-coupon bonds were down as much as 5/8 point.

Fifteen-year mortgage securities were down about 3/8 point at most. Balloon MBS, due in five or seven years, had similar losses. In both balloons and 15-year bonds, as with 30-year debt, the price erosion was more significant in the lower coupons that buyers had earlier been buying as a safe-haven from faster prepayments.

Willmann noted that his $320 million fund was broadly diversified to be more effective during a variety of interest- rate environments. He has not used hedge techniques such as buying principal-only securities or futures.

He has about one-quarter of the fund in adjustable-rate mortgage securities, one-quarter in project loans and half of the portfolio in 30-year single-family MBS that are mainly 7-1/2 percent and lower coupons.

Amid 30-year 7-1/2s, Government National Mortgage Association bonds were down 13/32 at 100-23/32, Federal National Mortgage Association bonds were off 9/32 at 100-27/32 and Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp bonds were 19/32 lower on the day at 100-24/32.

The 10-year Treasury note, in stark contrast, lost 30/32 to 98-06/32 to yield 6.37 percent. The note yield briefly touched down to 6.00 percent just over a week ago, when prepayment fears were more intense.
